segmentation.text: shall not cross an intersection diagonally
unless authorized by official traffic-control devices.

elements.justification: 'Pedestrian' is defined by DEF-NRS-484A-165 ('a person afoot, a person in a manual or motorized wheelchair, or a person on an electric personal assistive mobility device'); the run admits it as the aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-165::pedestrian, claimed whole and never expanded into class atoms.

'intersection' (DEF-NRS-484A-105: 'The area embraced within the prolongation or connection of the lateral curb lines') is st.intersection, 'the region where two roadways meet, bounded by the prolongation of their edges'; the alley-junction exclusion of the definition's (3) is made by the atom's own contract. rel.occupies ('a road user's footprint overlaps a lane / region') anchors the pedestrian in that intersection. 'diagonally' is a direction of the pedestrian's motion relative to the ways that meet there: the lanes that run into the intersection are read through st.lane_enters ('the intersection region a directed approach carrier runs into at its entrance end'; kind st.lane), and drv.motion.moving_across_carrier, whose contract compares the road user's velocity with a carrier's designated direction, is read at two tolerances on every such lane: across it with the tolerance that tells across from along, and not across it with the right-angle tolerance, so the motion is oblique to both crossing ways. st.lane_enters is not used for the subject's presence (that is rel.occupies) nor for governance.

An 'official traffic-control device' (DEF-NRS-484A-145) includes every 'marking ... placed or erected by a public authority ... for the purpose of regulating, warning or guiding traffic'; the marking that authorizes a pedestrian crossing is a crosswalk 'distinctly indicated for pedestrian crossing by lines or other markings on the surface' (DEF-NRS-484A-065 (2)), carried by st.crosswalk ('marked crossing ...; marked attribute') read with its marked attribute; rel.occupies anchors the pedestrian inside that marked crossing. st.crosswalk 'Not a stand-in for' clauses do not concern this use.

applicability: The subject is a pedestrian (ru.aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-165::pedestrian) whose footprint overlaps an intersection x (rel.occupies, st.intersection) into which at least one lane runs (st.lane_enters); the duty does not apply where LVMC_11_30_140_B_o1 or LVMC_11_30_140_B_o2 is engaged for the subject.
obligation: At each such observation: if the subject moves diagonally across x, that is, for every lane l with st.lane_enters(l, x), drv_motion_moving_across_carrier(subject, l) holds with parameters (p.halt_speed_tolerance, p.crossing_motion_cos) and does not hold with parameters (p.halt_speed_tolerance, p.right_angle_crossing_cos), then the subject's footprint overlaps a marked crosswalk (st.crosswalk with its marked attribute true). Otherwise compliant.

narrowings.why: 'cross ... diagonally' is read at each observation as the pedestrian, inside the intersection, moving oblique to every lane that runs into it (neither within the right-angle tolerance of across a lane nor along it); a crossing is judged by its motion at each observation, not as a corner-to-corner path.
'official' is read through the presence of the marking on the road: a marked crosswalk in the scene is presumed placed by a public authority.

scenarios.name: forbid
scenarios.narrative: Lanes running into intersection x run north-south and east-west; a pedestrian inside x walks north-east at 1.4 m/s, oblique to every entering lane, with no crosswalk under its footprint.

scenarios.name: permit
scenarios.narrative: A pedestrian inside x near its edge walks east at 1.4 m/s: across the north-south lanes at right angles, so the motion is not diagonal.

scenarios.name: idle
scenarios.narrative: The pedestrian walks along a sidewalk and its footprint overlaps no intersection.

scenarios.name: blind
scenarios.narrative: The pedestrian is inside x with no marked crosswalk under it, but its velocity is not observed, so whether it moves diagonally cannot be told.

scenarios.name: branch_1
scenarios.narrative: A pedestrian inside x walks north-east within a marked diagonal crosswalk.

param_proposals.name: p.halt_speed_tolerance
param_proposals.convention: the speed at or below which a sampled speed counts as no movement: the source's speed resolution
param_proposals.source: speed resolution of the acquisition standard's kinematic channel

param_proposals.name: p.crossing_motion_cos
param_proposals.convention: largest absolute cosine between a pedestrian's velocity and a carrier's designated direction at which the pedestrian counts as moving across the carrier rather than along it: motion more than about 20 degrees away from the direction of travel
param_proposals.source: pedestrian trajectory heading variability in naturalistic crossing studies

param_proposals.name: p.right_angle_crossing_cos
param_proposals.convention: largest absolute cosine between a pedestrian's velocity and a carrier's designated direction at which the motion counts as at right angles to the curb: within about 15 degrees of perpendicular
param_proposals.source: pedestrian trajectory heading variability in naturalistic crossing studies
